examination_method: Autopsy — Recent Activity / Event Logs module; filtered Event ID 4624
observation: Successful interactive logon by user account 'John' at 08:14:22 UTC. Logon type 2 (interactive). Source IP: local console.
interpretation: Suspect user account authenticated and established an interactive local session at the start of the incident window.
alternative_explanation: Could be a normal working-hours logon if the user routinely accesses the system at this time. No baseline available.
limitations: Log integrity not independently verified with external source; EVTX parsing relies on Autopsy's built-in parser.

examination_method: Autopsy — Event Logs; filtered Event ID 4672 (special privileges assigned)
observation: Special privileges (SeDebugPrivilege SeBackupPrivilege) assigned to new logon session for 'John' 3 minutes after initial logon.
interpretation: User obtained administrative-level privileges. This is expected for a local administrator account but notable given subsequent activity.
alternative_explanation: Standard administrator login — normal for IT staff. No direct evidence of privilege abuse from this event alone.
limitations: The presence of SeDebugPrivilege does not by itself prove malicious intent.

examination_method: Autopsy — File System browser; metadata view of $STANDARD_INFORMATION and $FILE_NAME attributes
observation: Last access timestamp updated at 08:19:33 UTC for company_data_Q3.xlsx located on the user's Desktop.
interpretation: A sensitive financial document was opened or accessed within 5 minutes of logon.
alternative_explanation: The $STANDARD_INFORMATION access timestamp can be updated by file system operations other than a user opening the file (e.g. AV scan thumbnail generation).
limitations: NTFS $STANDARD_INFORMATION access timestamps are unreliable on Windows systems where NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate is enabled. The $FILE_NAME timestamp did not update, which is consistent with typical NTFS behavior.

examination_method: Autopsy — Recent Activity module — Web History; parse of Chromium SQLite History database
observation: Google search query 'how to compress files windows command line' recorded at 08:22:11 UTC.
interpretation: User searched for a data compression technique 3 minutes after accessing the sensitive document. Consistent with preparing data for transfer.
alternative_explanation: User may have had a legitimate need to compress unrelated files. Without reviewing the search results pages or the zip contents this remains circumstantial.
limitations: Browser history timestamps use the WebKit epoch (microseconds since 1601-01-01). Autopsy's conversion was used; manual verification against raw DB is recommended.

examination_method: Autopsy — File System browser; $FILE_NAME creation timestamp (more reliable than $STANDARD_INFORMATION for creation events)
observation: Archive file 'exfil.zip' created at 08:24:44 UTC on the Desktop. File size: [to be recorded from lab]. Archive contents not directly viewable as file was later deleted.
interpretation: A compressed archive was created immediately after the sensitive document was accessed and the compression technique was searched. The filename 'exfil' is an unusual choice for legitimate activity.
alternative_explanation: Could be a coincidentally named test or backup archive unrelated to the data theft.
limitations: The archive contents cannot be confirmed — the file was deleted and the $R data stream was not recovered. Only the $I metadata was available.

examination_method: Autopsy — Recent Activity — Web History; URL and timestamp from Chromium History SQLite
observation: URL 'https://wetransfer.com' navigated at 08:26:00 UTC. Visit count: 1 (first visit from this profile).
interpretation: User navigated to WeTransfer — a public file-transfer service — 1 minute after creating the archive. WeTransfer is commonly used for unauthorized data transfer.
alternative_explanation: User could have navigated to WeTransfer for legitimate purposes (receiving a file from an external party).
limitations: Browser history records the URL but not the file content or recipient email. WeTransfer uploads are encrypted in transit and cannot be recovered from local artifacts.

examination_method: Autopsy — Recent Activity — Web History; upload confirmation URL pattern
observation: WeTransfer upload completion page URL recorded at 08:28:55 UTC. URL pattern matches WeTransfer post-upload confirmation page.
interpretation: An upload was completed on WeTransfer at 08:28:55 UTC — approximately 2 minutes after navigating to the site. This is consistent with the transfer of a file.
alternative_explanation: Could be a legitimate file upload (user receiving a confirmation rather than sending). URL pattern does not definitively distinguish sender from receiver confirmation.
limitations: URL pattern analysis is based on known WeTransfer URL structure. This interpretation may be affected by changes to WeTransfer's URL scheme. Contents of the upload cannot be verified from local artifacts.

examination_method: Autopsy — File System browser; deleted files / Recycle Bin analysis — $I metadata file parsed
observation: exfil.zip deleted to Recycle Bin at 08:31:07 UTC. Original path recovered from $I file: C:\Users\John\Desktop\exfil.zip. Original file size recorded in $I metadata.
interpretation: The archive was deleted from the Desktop 2 minutes after the suspected upload. Rapid deletion following transfer is consistent with deliberate anti-forensic behavior.
alternative_explanation: File deletion could be routine cleanup (user deletes temporary files regularly). Timing is circumstantial.
limitations: The $I file provides deletion metadata but not file contents. The $R data file was absent — consistent with permanent deletion or Recycle Bin emptying.

examination_method: Autopsy — Deleted Files analysis; $R file absence noted; Recycle Bin folder modification timestamp
observation: Recycle Bin $R data file for exfil.zip not present. Folder modification timestamp at 08:32:30 UTC indicates Recycle Bin was emptied or modified at this time.
interpretation: The Recycle Bin was emptied after the archive was placed there — permanently removing the file contents from immediately recoverable storage.
alternative_explanation: Recycle Bin may have been emptied by an automated cleanup policy rather than deliberate user action.
limitations: File content may be recoverable from unallocated disk space using file carving (not performed in this investigation). Timestamp is from folder $STANDARD_INFORMATION — less reliable.

examination_method: Autopsy — Event Logs; Event ID 4634 (logoff) paired with F-001 logon
observation: User 'John' logged off at 08:33:45 UTC. Total session duration: approximately 19 minutes and 23 seconds.
interpretation: Session was short and focused — the user performed a discrete set of actions and immediately terminated the session.
alternative_explanation: Short sessions may be normal for this user — no baseline behavioral data available.
limitations: Session duration analysis requires comparison with historical logon patterns which are not available in this investigation.

examination_method: Autopsy — Event Logs; Event ID 20001 (Plug and Play device installed)
observation: USB Plug and Play device connected at 09:05:22 UTC — 31 minutes after 'John' logged off. Device class: mass storage.
interpretation: A USB storage device was connected after the primary session. May represent a secondary exfiltration attempt or is an unrelated event.
alternative_explanation: USB insertion may be by a different user (no logon event between John's logoff and USB insertion in available logs). Event 20001 records device installation not user identity.
limitations: System event log does not record the user account context for PnP events in all Windows versions. The USB device identifier (VID/PID) should be examined further for prior connection history via setupapi.dev.log.

examination_method: Autopsy Tools > Make Timeline — full case timeline generated
observation: Autopsy generated a full file-system timeline covering the investigation period. 1247 total events recorded between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-14.
interpretation: Timeline provides comprehensive chronological view of file system activity corroborating the sequence identified in the key findings above.
alternative_explanation: Timeline generated from the image — does not account for events that occurred before the investigation period or artifacts overwritten in unallocated space.
limitations: Timeline completeness depends on the Autopsy ingest modules run and the file system metadata available. Deleted metadata records may be absent if overwritten.
